create.name: Gen Kelsang Chokyi
create.bio:
Gen Kelsang Chokyi is an American Buddhist nun in the New Kadampa Tradition and the resident teacher of the Kadampa Meditation Centers in Indianapolis and Bloomington, Indiana. She has studied under Geshe Kelsang Gyatso, the tradition's founder, for around two decades, and before coming to Indiana she was resident teacher at Kadampa centres in New Bedford, Massachusetts, San Diego and Providence, Rhode Island.

Her teaching is aimed at people who want to bring Buddhist ideas into ordinary life without needing to call themselves Buddhist. In Indianapolis she leads the Sunday morning class, where each session pairs a breathing meditation with a short teaching and a contemplation, currently working through mind-training (lojong) themes from Geshe Kelsang's book The New Eight Steps to Happiness. She also gives Saturday workshops for beginners on subjects such as acceptance, overthinking and meeting the holidays calmly, guides day retreats on Lamrim and Vajrasattva practice, and in 2027 is taking a monthly series of morning meditation workshops to Cincinnati. Her style is warm and practical, and she often draws on Geshe Kelsang's books as the basis for a course.

courses.title: Cultivating Inner Stability: Sunday Morning Meditation Class
courses.description: Her weekly drop-in class at the Indianapolis centre: a breathing meditation, a teaching and a guided contemplation, currently on the mind-training themes of The New Eight Steps to Happiness. Sessions can be taken singly or as a series, and members attend free.

courses.title: Beginner Workshop: The Art of Acceptance
courses.description: A two-hour Saturday morning workshop in Indianapolis on patient acceptance: how it differs from giving up, how to notice an unwelcome feeling without pushing it away or reacting, and simple ways to build that habit of mind. Based on Geshe Kelsang Gyatso's How to Solve Our Human Problems.

courses.title: Cincy Workshop: Discovering Strength Within
courses.description: The first of five Saturday morning meditation workshops she is leading in Cincinnati in 2027, open to complete beginners. This one looks at the habits of mind behind feeling let down or discouraged and how meditation can change the way we see ourselves and others.
